- When sentiment is high (≥0.85) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows a sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >+5% from prior), true outcome often overshoots and then corrects — cap forecast peak at 2–3% below true peak.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early periods of a 30-day forecast (especially days 1–5), especially when sentiment is low or volatile — add 0.5–1.5% to early forecast values.
- When sentiment history shows a clear downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive low sentiment values), model tends to lag — delay peak forecast by 1–2 days and adjust downward by 1–2%.
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion in the 10–15 day horizon — if forecast shows sustained upward trend, check for 3–5 day reversal in sentiment or price; if confirmed, reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model overreacts — suppress forecast increases by 1–2% for 2–3 days until sentiment stabilizes.
